subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Outdoor, Adventure, and Community Recreation Planning
essentialQuestion: How do I plan an activity that is genuinely worth the effort of getting there?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of planning a longer or more demanding outdoor activity in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply navigation, communication, and contingency planning in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving group planning and shared responsibility; correct it and explain why.
Connect cost, transport, permits, and access realities with environmental stewardship and shared-space responsibility and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Produce a complete plan for one guardian-approved outdoor or community activity — risk assessment, logistics, contingency, and stewardship — and carry it out if approved, or complete the equivalent local or indoor version.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Scale, distance, terrain, and duration are learner-set. A full indoor or home-area equivalent is available for any learner for whom the outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
